summary: Tested the 4-fix batch end-to-end: (A) new backend PATCH/DELETE /api/workloads/{id} and (B) frontend Planner summary + Previous-button styling + checklist text styling + history rename/delete. 8/8 pytest cases pass (rename happy path, delete happy path, bogus-id 404 for both verbs, auth-required 401 for both verbs, cross-user ownership returns 404 and admin's record stays, pydantic name 2-100 validation returns 422). Frontend: planner-prev-button is visually distinct (bg rgb(238,245,251), text rgb(18,89,165), class planner-prev); task spans show textDecoration=none, color rgb(27,94,32), fontWeight 600 when li.done; Prev disabled on stage01 and Next disabled on stage04; on stage04 planner-summary + 4 summary-{id} cards + PATTERN EXPANSION dark card + planner-reset-button all render; clicking reset clears all 16 checkboxes. History: rename pencil swaps row into input + Save/Cancel, Save sends PATCH and row re-renders with new name, Cancel reverts without saving. Delete triggers confirm, accept sends DELETE, row removed and history-count decrements by 1 (11 -> 10).
critical_code_review_comments: Review request references planner task test-ids as 'planner-task-stage01-0' but actual implementation uses step.id values ('current', 'package', 'destination', 'switch'), so the real ids are 'planner-task-current-0', 'planner-task-package-0', etc. Pattern matches planner-task-{stage}-{idx} but 'stage' is a semantic placeholder, not the literal string. Worth noting for future test authors but functionally correct and consistent with summary-{id} card ids.

resetChecklist in Planner only clears the done map; it does NOT navigate back to stage 01. The 'Start a new migration' button therefore leaves the user on stage 04 with the summary still visible (because showSummary = activeStep===3 || allComplete). Consider also calling setActiveStep(0) inside resetChecklist so the user visibly starts over.

App.js is a single ~100-line file with every route component inlined; the Planner render is a 30+ line single JSX expression on one line (lines 70-99). It renders fine but is near-unreadable; splitting Planner / History into their own files would help maintainability.

PATCH endpoint accepts only name; good. But Pydantic validator fires BEFORE the ObjectId existence check, so a PATCH with name='x' on a bogus id returns 422 (validation) instead of 404 - acceptable REST behavior but worth noting.
seed_data_creation: Backend tests create and delete TEST_ prefixed workloads for admin and TEST_<uuid>@example.com users; UI test renamed one existing admin workload to 'UI Renamed WL' then deleted it. Admin history ended at 10 saved workloads.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend: PATCH /api/workloads/{id} (name 2-100) and DELETE /api/workloads/{id} both work, require auth, scope by user_id (cross-user returns 404), and return 404 for bogus but valid ObjectIds. See /app/backend/tests/test_workload_crud.py. Frontend data-testids: planner-summary, summary-current|package|destination|switch, planner-reset-button, planner-prev-button (class planner-prev with blue accent), planner-task-{stepId}-{idx} where stepId is current|package|destination|switch (NOT stage01-04). History row test-ids: history-rename-{id}, history-delete-{id}, history-rename-input-{id}, history-save-{id}, history-cancel-{id}, history-count. Delete uses window.confirm so Playwright must register page.once('dialog', d.accept()).
rca of the issue: N/A - all 4 fixes verified working. Minor nit: planner-reset-button does not reset activeStep back to 0, so user remains on stage 04 after reset. Not blocking.
